name: Vigil
blurb: A multi-monitor, themeable greetd greeter that renders straight to KMS/DRM with Slint, no compositor required.

media.alt: Vigil running on three monitors at once, one rotated to portrait. The login panel follows the pointer from screen to screen.

problem: Graphical Wayland greeters need a compositor, so a routine desktop upgrade can break the one thing that must never break: login.
how: Vigil is its own display backend. One Rust binary drives every monitor straight over KMS/DRM and draws an independent, themeable scene on each.
proof: The full login flow is tested end to end in QEMU.

name: swivel
blurb: One set of peripherals shared by several machines through a small device.
problem: Two full desks, one good headset, and every extra machine means more cables and more pairing.
how: swivel shares one set of peripherals across several machines. There is no central node: the small device in the middle is just another peer, each device has its own authority, and a new machine joins through any existing member.
proof: Designed through written decision records and exercised in its own test harness.

name: hypr-DE
blurb: An alpha Wayland desktop composed from small, separately versioned parts.
problem: A desktop assembled from dozens of tools drifts apart, and nobody can say which part owns what.
how: hypr-DE is a Wayland desktop built from small, separately versioned repos. Machine-readable registries define who owns what, and releases ship as signed Arch and Fedora packages.
proof: Alpha, and honest about it: the supporting tools stabilize first.

media.alt: The hypr-DE desktop: a terminal, a launcher opening a file manager, a workspace switch, and a live light and dark theme toggle.

name: hyprstate
blurb: Hyprland session state machine covering lid, monitor profiles, lock, suspend, and USB wake.
problem: Lid, monitors, lock, suspend and USB wake all fight over the same session, and each fix breaks another.
how: One event-sourced state machine over Hyprland, logind and UPower, with a reconciler that re-asserts the hard invariants.
proof: Effects are isolated from a pure transition function, so the logic is testable.

name: dials
blurb: A native settings app for hyprstate monitor profiles.
problem: Monitor layouts on Wayland are config files you edit blind.
how: dials is a native Slint app. Drag monitors into place, set mode, scale and rotation, and it writes the monitor profiles that hyprstate applies.

media.alt: The dials Displays page: two monitors dragged into a new arrangement, then the page flips between dark and light.

name: hyprhands
blurb: Fast, safe hands on a Hyprland desktop for agent loops: capture, accessibility tree, input, and owner takeover detection.
problem: An agent driving a desktop needs eyes and hands, without trampling the person sitting at it.
how: Capture, accessibility tree and input over a small framed stdio protocol, with detection for when the owner takes back the mouse.

name: open-comfort-engine
blurb: Thermostats that learn how warm people like it from too hot / too cold votes, and drift toward idle to save energy.
problem: People know when they are too hot or too cold. They do not know what setpoint they want.
how: Thermostats learn preferred warmth from plain votes, and drift toward idle to save energy.
proof: A language-neutral spec, a TypeScript reference, and Node-RED nodes.

name: slint-kit
blurb: Shared Slint theme and widgets fed by Material You colors.

name: linux-multi-theme-toggle
blurb: High-performance async theme switching for Hyprland desktops with Material You color schemes.

name: marble-run-parts
blurb: Connector spec and OpenSCAD library for tube marble run sets.

name: pm-loop
blurb: A PM loop workflow for coordinating AI coding agents.

name: sni-watcher
blurb: Standalone StatusNotifierWatcher daemon that keeps tray items alive across status bar restarts.

name: steam-notes
blurb: Notes on Steam client internals: shortcut appids, CEF debugging, flatpak pitfalls, SteamOS persistence.
